🤝 Ethics & Safety

AI alignment

In simple words

Making sure an AI tries to do what people really intend and value, not just what they literally said.

The work of making AI systems pursue the goals people really intend, in safe and honest ways — not just what their instructions or rewards literally say. It matters more as AI gets more capable, and it is an open research problem: nobody has a complete solution yet.

Example. In old stories, a genie grants wishes word for word, with terrible results. Alignment research tries to make sure AI understands what you mean, not just what you say.

Lessons that teach it

  • Lesson 11: Can You Trust AI?

Related words

  • Artificial general intelligence (AGI)A possible future AI that could learn almost any mental task a human can; it doesn't exist yet.
  • Reward hackingWhen an AI finds a loophole that earns lots of reward without doing what its designers really wanted.
  • Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)A way to make a chatbot more helpful: people rate its answers, and those ratings become its reward in reinforcement learning.
  • Red teamingTesting an AI by trying hard, on purpose, to make it fail or misbehave, so the problems can be fixed.
